subject: playwright
title: Assertions
description: Web-first assertions that retry, generic ones that do not, soft assertions, and what toBeVisible really means.

content.title: Two kinds of expect
content.body: expect(locator) is web-first: it polls until the condition holds or the timeout expires, and must be awaited. expect(value) is a plain Jest-style assertion on something you already read — it checks once and cannot recover from a timing gap.

content.title: The awaited form
content.body: Forgetting the await is the most common mistake in a Playwright review: the assertion becomes a floating promise and the test passes no matter what.

content.title: Good practice
content.body: expect.soft() records a failure and keeps going, so one run can report every broken assertion on the page instead of only the first. The test still fails at the end.

exercises.question: This test passes even when the alert never appears. Why?

answers.text: Line 2 is not awaited, so the assertion is a dangling promise nobody checks
toHaveText only warns, it never fails
Line 1 should use force: true
getByRole('alert') matches everything

exercises.explanation: Every web-first assertion returns a promise. Without await the test finishes first and the rejection surfaces — if at all — as an unhandled promise warning.

exercises.question: What does toBeVisible() require?

answers.text: The element is in the DOM and has a non-empty bounding box
The element is scrolled into the viewport
The element is not covered by any other element
The element has opacity greater than zero

exercises.explanation: Visibility is about layout, not the viewport: an element below the fold is visible. Interception is checked at action time, and opacity: 0 still counts as visible.

exercises.question: The locator matches three rows. What does this assert?

answers.text: That the three items have exactly those texts, in that order
That at least one item matches one of the strings
It throws a strict mode violation
That the concatenated text equals the joined array

exercises.explanation: Passing an array asserts the whole collection, count included. Strict mode applies to actions, not assertions — which is why this is allowed.

exercises.question: A test containing only failing expect.soft() assertions still ends as failed.
exercises.explanation: Soft assertions defer the failure to the end of the test rather than cancelling it. They are for collecting several problems in one run, not for ignoring them.

exercises.question: Complete the assertion that waits for the dialog to go away.

answers.text: not
never
no
without

exercises.explanation: not keeps the retrying behaviour: it polls until the dialog is gone. toBeHidden() says the same thing and reads better when the element stays in the DOM.

exercises.question: The row should be removed from the DOM entirely. Which assertion says that?

answers.text: await expect(row).toHaveCount(0)
await expect(row).toBeHidden()
await expect(row).not.toBeVisible()
expect(await row.isVisible()).toBe(false)

exercises.explanation: toBeHidden and not.toBeVisible both pass for an element that is merely invisible. Only toHaveCount(0) distinguishes "gone" from "display: none".

exercises.question: Complete the visual assertion.

answers.text: toHaveScreenshot
toMatchImage
toLookLike
toBeScreenshot

exercises.explanation: toHaveScreenshot retries too — it re-takes the screenshot until two consecutive captures are identical, which is what stops animations producing false diffs.

exercises.topic: Asserting on a value that will change
exercises.question: Which version tolerates the total updating a moment after the click?

answers.text: B — the locator assertion polls until the text matches
A — innerText waits for the element automatically
Both, since innerText auto-waits
Neither without an explicit timeout

exercises.explanation: innerText() does auto-wait for the element, but it reads once — the value it returns is a snapshot, and the assertion around it cannot retry.

exercises.question: Playwright · assertions
exercises.back: The second argument becomes the failure message in the report
exercises.explanation: Cheap and high value in CI: the reporter shows your sentence instead of only the locator and the diff.

exercises.question: A web-first assertion fails after 5 seconds although the test timeout is 30. Why?

answers.text: Each assertion has its own timeout, 5 s by default
The test timeout only applies to hooks
Assertions inherit a quarter of the test timeout
The browser closed the page

exercises.explanation: expect.timeout is configured separately from test timeout. Override per call — toBeVisible({ timeout: 15_000 }) — or globally in the config.

exercises.question: toHaveText normalises whitespace, so extra spaces and line breaks in the markup do not fail the assertion.
exercises.explanation: Leading, trailing and repeated whitespace are collapsed. Use toHaveText(/regex/) when you need to be stricter, or toContainText for a substring.

exercises.question: What is wrong with this attempt to prove an error banner never shows?

answers.text: Nothing — this is the correct pattern
It passes immediately, before the banner would have had time to appear
not cannot be combined with toBeVisible
getByRole('alert') needs a name

exercises.explanation: A negative assertion is satisfied the instant it is true, which is straight after the click. Assert the positive outcome first — the success toast, the new row — and then the absence.
